basics.name: Han Liu
basics.label: Researcher
basics.summary: Computational physicist at St. Anthony Falls Laboratory, University of Minnesota. Research focused on building high-fidelity CFD solvers for multiphase turbulent flows, GPU-accelerated computing, and quantum-inspired methods for fluid mechanics. Experience delivering digital twin platforms for industrial applications.

work.name: Claros Technologies
work.summary: End-to-end CFD digital twin for PFAS chemical reactor: parametric geometry, simulation, data generation, optimization, and chemical kinetics integration.

work.name: Dynamic Dimension Technologies (DDT), LLC
work.summary: Ocean wave modeling platform with shoaling, bathymetry, vehicle dynamics, and synthetic data generation for surrogate models.

work.name: St. Anthony Falls Laboratory, University of Minnesota
work.summary: Built incompressible CFD solver with AMR, CLSVOF interface tracking, and cut-cell boundaries on AMReX. Ported Fortran HPC code to C++/CUDA multi-GPU. Developed quantum-classical hybrid frameworks for Navier-Stokes acceleration.

work.name: St. Anthony Falls Laboratory, University of Minnesota
work.summary: Developed CLSVOF interface tracking for high-density-ratio multiphase flows. Simulated COVID-19 airborne transmission (Featured Article, Physics of Fluids). Researched oil spill dynamics and hydrokinetic turbine optimization.
